# htop

![Screenshot of htop](docs/images/screenshot.png?raw=true)

## Introduction

`htop` is a cross-platform interactive process viewer.

`htop` allows scrolling the list of processes vertically and horizontally to see their full command lines and related information like memory and CPU consumption.
Also system wide information, like load average or swap usage, is shown.

The information displayed is configurable through a graphical setup and can be sorted and filtered interactively.

Tasks related to processes (e.g. killing and renicing) can be done without entering their PIDs.

For more information and details visit [htop.dev](https://htop.dev).

## Usage

See the manual page (`man htop`) or the help menu (`h` or `F1` inside `htop`) for a list of supported key commands.

### Quick Start

Some common actions to get you started with `htop`:

- Search processes: press `/`
- Filter processes: press `\`
- Toggle tree view: press `t`
- Change process sort column: press `.`
- Kill a process: select the process and press `k`

## Command-Line Options

- `-d DELAY` : Delay between updates, in tenths of a second
- `-C` : Start in monochrome mode
- `-F` : Filter by command name
- `-h` : Display help and exit
- `-p PID[,PID...]` : Show only the given PIDs
- `-s COLUMN` : Sort by specified column
- `-t` : Start in tree view mode
- `-u USERNAME` : Show only processes of a given user
- `-v` : Print version and exit
- `-H` : Show threads

## pcp-htop

`pcp-htop` is a version of `htop` built using the Performance Co-Pilot (PCP) Metrics API, allowing display of values from arbitrary metrics.

## License

GNU General Public License, version 2 (GPL-2.0) or, at your option, any later version.

.TP
\fB\-d \-\-delay=DELAY\fR
Delay between updates, in tenths of a second. If the delay value is

Commonly used to indicate values as a percentage using a "%"
.I suffix
value and to provide the base unit of measurement.
Note that since PCP maintains units for metrics, for those
metrics that have dimension in "space" (bytes, kilobytes,
megabytes, etc), a suffix will be automatically appended.
.SH "COLUMNS"
The following is an example configuration for a new column
showing open file descriptors for each process:
.LP
.ft CR
.nf
.in +0.5i
[openfds]
heading = FDS
caption = FDCOUNT
description = Open file descriptors
metric = proc.fd.count
width = 3
.in
.fi
.ft 1
.LP
A configuration file can contain multiple column definitions.
Each definition begins with a identifying name enclosed
by square brackets \-
.I openfds
in this example, and the same rules apply as described above
for meter names.
.LP
Each column must specify a metric.
Optional parameters can also be set.
.TP 5
.B metric
As with meters, the metric value must be either a PCP metric
name as listed by
.BR pminfo (1)
or a derived metric.
The metric must have an instance domain (set of values) and
that instance domain must map to the set of processes with
the instance identifier being PIDs (process identifiers).
Typically this will be metrics from the
.I proc
or
.I hotproc
namespace (\c
.BR pmdaproc (1)),
but metrics from other domains (\c
.BR pmdabpf (1),
etc) that have per-process values are equally applicable.
.TP
.B width
Column width to use when displaying values for the metric.
A negative value can be used to specify left alignment.
An upper column limit of 28 characters is enforced.
The default column width is 5 characters.
.TP
.B heading
The short title that will be displayed at the head of the
column \- usually a short, cryptic, all uppercase string.
.TP
.B caption
A short identifying word presented to users on the Setup
screen under both the Available and Active Columns lists.
.TP
.B description
Text that assists users to understand the meaning of this
column when it is being presented via the Setup screen in
the Available Columns list.
.SH "SEE ALSO"
.BR pcp-htop (1),
.BR pminfo (1),
.BR pmcd (1),
.BR pmdaproc (1),
.BR pmdabpf (1)
and
.BR pmRegisterDerived (3).
.SH "AUTHORS"
.B htop
was originally developed by Hisham Muhammad.
Nowadays it is maintained by the community at <htop@groups.io>.
.LP
.B pcp-htop
is maintained as a collaboration between the <htop@groups.io> and <pcp@groups.io>
communities, and forms part of the Performance Co-Pilot suite of tools.

.TP
.B Up, Alt-k
Select (highlight) the previous process in the process list. Scroll the list
if necessary.
.TP
.B Down, Alt-j
Select (highlight) the next process in the process list. Scroll the list if
necessary.
.TP
.B Left, Alt-h
Scroll the process list left.
.TP
.B Right, Alt-l
Scroll the process list right.
.TP
.B PgUp, PgDn
Scroll the process list up or down one window.
.TP
.B Home
Scroll to the top of the process list and select the first process.
.TP
.B End
Scroll to the bottom of the process list and select the last process.
.TP
.B Ctrl-A, ^
Scroll left to the beginning of the process entry (i.e. beginning of line).
.TP
.B Ctrl-E, $
Scroll right to the end of the process entry (i.e. end of line).
.TP
.B Space
Tag or untag a process. Commands that can operate on multiple processes,
like "kill", will then apply over the list of tagged processes, instead
of the currently highlighted one.
.TP
.B c
Tag the current process and its children. Commands that can operate on multiple
processes, like "kill", will then apply over the list of tagged processes,
instead of the currently highlighted one.
.TP
.B U
Untag all processes (remove all tags added with the Space or c keys).
.TP
.B s
Trace process system calls: if strace(1) is installed, pressing this key
will attach it to the currently selected process, presenting a live
update of system calls issued by the process.
.TP
.B l
Display open files for a process: if lsof(1) is installed, pressing this key
will display the list of file descriptors opened by the process.
.TP
.B w
Display the command line of the selected process in a separate screen, wrapped
onto multiple lines as needed.
.TP
.B x
Display the active file locks of the selected process in a separate screen.
.TP
.B F1, h, ?
Go to the help screen
.TP
.B F2, S
Go to the setup screen, where you can configure the meters displayed at the top
of the screen, set various display options, choose among color schemes, and
select which columns are displayed, in which order.
.TP
.B F3, /
Incrementally search the command lines of all the displayed processes. The
currently selected (highlighted) command will update as you type. While in
search mode, pressing F3 will cycle through matching occurrences.
Pressing Shift-F3 will cycle backwards.

Alternatively the search can be started by simply typing the command
you are looking for, although for the first character normal key
bindings take precedence.
.TP
.B F4, \\\\
Incremental process filtering: type in part of a process command line and
only processes whose names match will be shown. To cancel filtering,
enter the Filter option again and press Esc.
The matching is done case-insensitive. Terms are fixed strings (no regex).
You can separate multiple terms with "|".
.TP
.B F5, t
Tree view: organize processes by parenthood, and layout the relations
between them as a tree. Toggling the key will switch between tree and
your previously selected sort view. Selecting a sort view will exit
tree view.
.TP
.B F6, <, >
Selects a field for sorting, also accessible through < and >.
The current sort field is indicated by a highlight in the header.
.TP
.B F7, ]
Increase the selected process's priority (subtract from 'nice' value).
This can only be done by the superuser.
.TP
.B F8, [
Decrease the selected process's priority (add to 'nice' value)
.TP
.B Shift-F7, }
Increase the selected process's autogroup priority (subtract from autogroup 'nice' value).
This can only be done by the superuser.
.TP
.B Shift-F8, {
Decrease the selected process's autogroup priority (add to autogroup 'nice' value)
.TP
.B F9, k
"Kill" process: sends a signal which is selected in a menu, to one or a group
of processes. If processes were tagged, sends the signal to all tagged processes.
If none is tagged, sends to the currently selected process.
.TP
.B F10, q
Quit
.TP
.B I
Invert the sort order: if sort order is increasing, switch to decreasing, and
vice-versa.
.TP
.B +, \-, *
When in tree view mode, expand or collapse subtree. When a subtree is collapsed
a "+" sign shows to the left of the process name.
Pressing "*" will expand or collapse all children of PIDs without parents, so
typically PID 1 (init) and PID 2 (kthreadd on Linux, if kernel threads are shown).
.TP
.B a (on multiprocessor machines)
Set CPU affinity: mark which CPUs a process is allowed to use.
.TP
.B u
Show only processes owned by a specified user.
.TP
.B N
Sort by PID.
.TP
.B M
Sort by memory usage (top compatibility key).
.TP
.B P
Sort by processor usage (top compatibility key).
.TP
.B T
Sort by time (top compatibility key).
.TP
.B F
"Follow" process: if the sort order causes the currently selected process
to move in the list, make the selection bar follow it. This is useful for
monitoring a process: this way, you can keep a process always visible on
screen. When a movement key is used, "follow" loses effect.
.TP
.B K
Hide kernel threads: prevent the threads belonging the kernel to be
displayed in the process list. (This is a toggle key.)
.TP
.B H
Hide user threads: on systems that represent them differently than ordinary
processes (such as recent NPTL-based systems), this can hide threads from
userspace processes in the process list. (This is a toggle key.)
.TP
.B O
Hide containerized processes: prevent processes running in a container
from being displayed in the process list. (This is a toggle key.)
.TP
.B p
Show full paths to running programs, where applicable. (This is a toggle key.)
.TP
.B Z
Pause/resume process updates.
.TP
.B m
Merge exe, comm and cmdline, where applicable. (This is a toggle key.)
.TP
.B Ctrl-L
Refresh: redraw screen and recalculate values.
.TP
.B Numbers
PID search: type in process ID and the selection highlight will be moved to it.
.PD
.SH "COLUMNS"
The following columns can display data about each process. A value of '\-' in
all the rows indicates that a column is unsupported on your system, or
currently unimplemented in
.BR htop .
The names below are the ones used in the
"Available Columns" section of the setup screen. If a different name is
shown in
.BR htop 's
main screen, it is shown below in parenthesis.
.TP 5
.B Command
The full command line of the process (i.e. program name and arguments).

If the option 'Merge exe, comm and cmdline in Command' (toggled by the 'm' key)
is active, the executable path (/proc/[pid]/exe) and the command name
(/proc/[pid]/comm) are also shown merged with the command line, if available.

The program basename is highlighted if set in the configuration. Additional
highlighting can be configured for stale executables (cf. EXE column below).

The Command column should be the last column in each screen as can get very long
and profits from being able to extend its length dynamically.

Additional color highlighting:
.RS
.IP \[bu] 2
Magenta: regular process command names
.IP \[bu] 2
Bold blue: userland thread names
.IP \[bu] 2
Bold gray: kernel threads or processes with no command name
.RE
.TP
.B COMM
The command name of the process obtained from /proc/[pid]/comm, if readable.

Requires Linux kernel 2.6.33 or newer.
.TP
.B EXE
The abbreviated basename of the executable of the process, obtained from
/proc/[pid]/exe, if readable. htop is able to read this file on linux for ALL
the processes only if it has the capability CAP_SYS_PTRACE or root privileges.

The basename is marked in red if the executable used to run the process has
been replaced or deleted on disk since the process started. The information is
obtained by processing the contents of /proc/[pid]/exe.

Furthermore the basename is marked in yellow if any library is reported as having
been replaced or deleted on disk since it was last loaded. The information is
obtained by processing the contents of /proc/[pid]/maps.

When deciding the color the replacement of the main executable always takes
precedence over replacement of any other library. If only the memory map indicates
a replacement of the main executable, this will show as if any other library had
been replaced or deleted.

This additional color markup can be configured in the "Display Options" section of
the setup screen.

Displaying EXE requires CAP_SYS_PTRACE and PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCRED.
.TP
.B PID
The process ID.
.TP
.B STATE (S)
The state of the process:
   \fBS\fR for sleeping
   \fBI\fR for idle (longer inactivity than sleeping on platforms that distinguish)
   \fBR\fR for running
   \fBD\fR for disk sleep (uninterruptible)
   \fBZ\fR for zombie (waiting for parent to read its exit status)
   \fBT\fR for traced or suspended (e.g by SIGTSTP)
</output>

.TP
.B PPID
The parent process ID.
.TP
.B PGRP
The process's group ID.
.TP
.B SESSION (SID)
The process's session ID.
.TP
.B TTY
The controlling terminal of the process.
.TP
.B TPGID
The process ID of the foreground process group of the controlling terminal.
.TP
.B MINFLT
The number of page faults happening in the main memory.
.TP
.B CMINFLT
The number of minor faults for the process's waited-for children (see MINFLT above).
.TP
.B MAJFLT
The number of page faults happening out of the main memory.
.TP
.B CMAJFLT
The number of major faults for the process's waited-for children (see MAJFLT above).
.TP
.B UTIME (UTIME+)
The user CPU time, which is the amount of time the process has spent executing
on the CPU in user mode (i.e. everything but system calls), measured in clock
ticks.
.TP
.B STIME (STIME+)
The system CPU time, which is the amount of time the kernel has spent
executing system calls on behalf of the process, measured in clock ticks.
.TP
.B CUTIME (CUTIME+)
The children's user CPU time, which is the amount of time the process's
waited-for children have spent executing in user mode (see UTIME above).
.TP
.B CSTIME (CSTIME+)
The children's system CPU time, which is the amount of time the kernel has spent
executing system calls on behalf of all the process's waited-for children (see
STIME above).
.TP
.B PRIORITY (PRI)
The kernel's internal priority for the process, usually just its nice value
plus twenty. Different for real-time processes.
.TP
.B NICE (NI)
The nice value of a process, from 19 (low priority) to -20 (high priority). A
high value means the process is being nice, letting others have a higher
relative priority. The usual OS permission restrictions for adjusting priority apply.
.TP
.B STARTTIME (START)
The time the process was started.
.TP
.B PROCESSOR (CPU)
The ID of the CPU the process last executed on.
.TP
.B M_VIRT (VIRT)
The size of the virtual memory of the process.
.TP
.B M_RESIDENT (RES)
The resident set size (text + data + stack) of the process (i.e. the size of the
process's used physical memory).
.TP
.B M_SHARE (SHR)
The size of the process's shared pages.
.TP
.B M_TRS (CODE)
The text resident set size of the process (i.e. the size of the process's
executable instructions).
.TP
.B M_DRS (DATA)
The data resident set size (data + stack) of the process (i.e. the size of anything
except the process's executable instructions).
.TP
.B M_LRS (LIB)
The library size of the process.
.TP
.B M_SWAP (SWAP)
The size of the process's swapped pages.
.TP
.B M_PSS (PSS)
The proportional set size, same as M_RESIDENT but each page is divided by the
number of processes sharing it.
.TP
.B M_M_PSSWP (PSSWP)
The proportional swap share of this mapping, unlike M_SWAP this does not take
into account swapped out page of underlying shmem objects.
.TP
.B ST_UID (UID)
The user ID of the process owner.
.TP
.B PERCENT_CPU (CPU%)
The percentage of the CPU time that the process is currently using.
This is the default way to represent CPU usage in Linux. Each process can
consume up to 100% which means the full capacity of the core it is running
on. This is sometimes called "Irix mode" e.g. in
.BR top (1).
.TP
.B PERCENT_NORM_CPU (NCPU%)
The percentage of the CPU time that the process is currently using normalized
by CPU count. This is sometimes called "Solaris mode" e.g. in
.BR top (1).
.TP
.B PERCENT_MEM (MEM%)
The percentage of memory the process is currently using (based on the process's
resident memory size, see M_RESIDENT above).
.TP
.B USER
The username of the process owner, or the user ID if the name can't be
determined.

On Linux the username is highlighted if the process has elevated privileges,
i.e. if it has been started from binaries with file capabilities set or
retained Linux capabilities, via the ambient set, after switching from the
root user.

Additional color highlighting:
.RS
.IP \[bu] 2
Magenta: elevated privilege processes
.IP \[bu] 2
Bold gray: processes owned by other users
.IP \[bu] 2
White (default): processes owned by the current user
.RE
.TP
.B TIME (TIME+)
The time, measured in clock ticks that the process has spent in user and system
time (see UTIME, STIME above).
.TP
.B NLWP
The number of Light-Weight Processes (=threads) in the process.
.TP
.B TGID
The thread group ID.
.TP
.B CTID
OpenVZ container ID, a.k.a virtual environment ID.
.TP
.B VPID
OpenVZ process ID.
.TP
.B VXID
VServer process ID.
.TP
.B RCHAR (RD_CHAR)
The number of bytes the process has read.
.TP
.B WCHAR (WR_CHAR)
The number of bytes the process has written.
.TP
.B SYSCR (RD_SYSC)
The number of read(2) syscalls for the process.
.TP
.B SYSCW (WR_SYSC)
The number of write(2) syscalls for the process.
.TP
.B RBYTES (IO_RBYTES)
Bytes of read(2) I/O for the process.
.TP
.B WBYTES (IO_WBYTES)
Bytes of write(2) I/O for the process.
.TP
.B CNCLWB (IO_CANCEL)
Bytes of cancelled write(2) I/O.
.TP
.B IO_READ_RATE (DISK READ)
The I/O rate of read(2) in bytes p
</output_head>

 cgroup the process is in. For a shortened view see the CCGROUP column below.
.TP
.B CCGROUP
Shortened view of the cgroup name that the process is in.
This performs some pattern-based replacements to shorten the displayed string and thus condense the information.
   \fB/*.slice\fR is shortened to \fB/[*]\fR (exceptions below)
   \fB/system.slice\fR is shortened to \fB/[S]\fR
   \fB/user.slice\fR is shortened to \fB/[U]\fR
   \fB/user-*.slice\fR is shortened to \fB/[U:*]\fR (directly preceding \fB/[U]\fR before dropped)
   \fB/machine.slice\fR is shortened to \fB/[M]\fR
   \fB/machine-*.scope\fR is shortened to \fB/[SNC:*]\fR (SNC: systemd nspawn container), uppercase for the monitor
   \fB/lxc.monitor.*\fR is shortened to \fB/[LXC:*]\fR
   \fB/lxc.payload.*\fR is shortened to \fB/[lxc:*]\fR
   \fB/*.scope\fR is shortened to \fB/!*\fR
   \fB/*.service\fR is shortened to \fB/*\fR (suffix removed)

Encountered escape sequences (e.g. from systemd) inside the cgroup name are not decoded.
.TP
.B OOM
OOM killer score.
.TP
.B CTXT
Incremental sum of voluntary and nonvoluntary context switches.
.TP
.B IO_PRIORITY (IO)
The I/O scheduling class followed by the priority if the class supports it:
   \fBR\fR for Realtime
   \fBB\fR for Best-effort
   \fBid\fR for Idle
.TP
.B PERCENT_CPU_DELAY (CPUD%)
The percentage of time spent waiting for a CPU (while runnable). Requires CAP_NET_ADMIN.
.TP
.B PERCENT_IO_DELAY (IOD%)
The percentage of time spent waiting for the completion of synchronous block I/O. Requires CAP_NET_ADMIN.
.TP
.B PERCENT_SWAP_DELAY (SWAPD%)
The percentage of time spent swapping in pages. Requires CAP_NET_ADMIN.
.TP
.B AGRP
The autogroup identifier for the process. Requires Linux CFS to be enabled.
.TP
.B ANI
The autogroup nice value for the process autogroup. Requires Linux CFS to be enabled.
.TP
.B All other flags
Currently unsupported (always displays '-').
.SH "EXTERNAL LIBRARIES"
While
.B htop
depends on most of the libraries it uses at build time there are two
noteworthy exceptions to this rule. These exceptions both relate to
data displayed in meters displayed in the header of
.B htop
and were intentionally created as optional runtime dependencies instead.
These exceptions are described below:
.TP
.B libsystemd
The bindings for libsystemd are used in the SystemD meter to determine
the number of active services and the overall system state. Looking for
the functions to determine these information at runtime allows for
builds to support these meters without forcing the package manager
to install these libraries on systems that otherwise don't use systemd.

Summary: no build time dependency, optional runtime dependency on
.B libsystemd
via dynamic loading, with
.B systemctl(1)
fallback.
.TP
.B libsensors
The bindings for libsensors are used for the CPU temperature readings
in the CPU usage meters if displaying the temperature is enabled through
the setup screen. In order for
.B htop
to show these temperatures correctly though, a proper configuration
of libsensors through its usual configuration files is assumed and that
all CPU cores correspond to temperature sensors from the
.B coretemp
driver with core 0 corresponding to a sensor labelled "Core 0". The
package temperature may be given as "Package id 0". If missing it is
inferred as the maximum value from the available per-core readings.

Summary: build time dependency on
.B libsensors(3)
C header files, optional runtime dependency on
.B libsensors(3)
via dynamic loading.
.SH "CONFIG FILES"
By default
.B htop
reads its configuration from the XDG-compliant path
.IR ~/.config/htop/htoprc .
The configuration file is overwritten upon clean exit by
.BR htop 's
in-program Setup configuration, so it should not be hand-edited.
If no user configuration exists
.B htop
tries to read the system-wide configuration from
.I @sysconfdir@/htoprc
and as a last resort, falls back to its hard coded defaults.
.LP
You may override the location of the configuration file using the $HTOPRC
environment variable (so you can have multiple configurations for different
machines that share the same home directory, for example).
.LP
The
.B pcp-htop
utility makes use of
.I htoprc
in a similar way.
However,
.B pcp-htop
reads its configuration from a path more conventionally used by
Performance Co-Pilot tools,
.IR ~/.pcp/htop/htoprc ,
in order to provide separate configuration when both
.B htop
and
.B pcp-htop
are installed and in use.
.B pcp-htop
supports additional configuration files below the same directory
allowing new meters, columns and screen tabs to be added via the
Setup screen (F2).
This displays additional Available Meters, Available Column and
Screen Tabs for each meter, column or screen configuration file.
.LP
These
.B pcp-htop
configuration files are read once at startup.
The format of these files is described in detail in the
.BR pcp-htop (5)
manual page.
.LP
This functionality makes available many thousands of Performance
Co-Pilot metrics for display by
.BR pcp-htop ,

.SH "DESCRIPTION"
.B pcp-htop
is a customizable performance metrics reporting tool.
It has a dynamic architecture, where a set of configuration files
provide additional, optional meters and columns to extend the fixed
set of display options provided by regular
.BR htop .
.LP
These configuration files can be provided from both system-wide
locations (first
.I @sysconfdir@/pcp/htop
then
.IR @datarootdir@/pcp/htop )
and below the user's home directory (usually
.IR ~/.config/htop ).
Within these locations the
.I meters
and
.I columns
are scanned for dynamic Meter and Column specifications.
.LP
Meters are displayed in the top part of the
.B pcp-htop
window, and columns are displayed in the lower part.
Meters tend to display system-wide metrics, and Columns
display metrics about individual processes.
.LP

Both formats follow the common ini-style. Blank lines are ignored.
Lines starting with the "#" character are treated as comments.

.LP
.ft CR
.nf
.in +0.5i
[redisclient]
caption = Redis clients
type = bar
blocked.metric = redis.blocked_clients
blocked.color = blue
blocked.label = blk
clients.metric = redis.connected_clients
clients.color = green
clients.label = conn
.in
.fi
.ft 1
.LP
A configuration file can contain multiple meter definitions.
Each definition begins with a identifying name enclosed by
square brackets \-
.I redisclient
in this example.
The name is used internally within
.B pcp-htop
and must be unique, must begin with an alphabetic character,
and may subsequently only contain alphanumeric characters or
the underscore character.
No whitespace or other characters are allowed.
.LP

will be displayed to the user.
.TP 5

has been selected.
A truncated version of the
.I caption
will also be displayed (followed by a colon) on the primary
display while the meter is updating.
.TP
.B description
This can be used to provide more detail during the meter
selection process on the Setup screen, and if present it is
displayed in the "Available Meters" column.
If not present, the
.B caption
will be used for this.
If neither is present, the internal (mandatory)
.B name
will be used.
.TP

The associated value must be one of
.IR bar ,
.IR text ,
.IR graph ,
or

If no value is provided for a dynamic meter, the default value of

content.text: The program is an interactive process viewer. I’ve mapped its CLI validation, configuration format, and main screens through direct runs. I’ll now implement those behaviors using Python’s standard-library curses support and Linux `/proc` data, with no runtime dependency on the reference binary.

from pathlib import Path
base=Path('/tmp/htop-observations')

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

# Only Python's standard library is required (including curses on Linux).
python3 -c 'import curses, zipapp'
python3 -m zipapp src -p '/usr/bin/env python3' -o executable
chmod +x executable
EOF

# Setup row labels, linked to persistent settings. None denotes an explanatory row.

def atoi(s, default=0):
    m=re.match(r'\s*([+-]?\d+)',str(s))
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else default


def sort_direction(col):
    return 1 if col in ['PID','PPID','PGRP','SESSION','TTY','TPGID','ST_UID','USER','Command','COMM','EXE','CWD','STATE','NICE','PRIORITY','PROCESSOR','TGID','STARTTIME','CONTAINER','CGROUP','CCGROUP','SECATTR','AUTOGROUP_ID','AUTOGROUP_NICE','SCHEDULERPOLICY'] else -1


def new_screen(name='Main',fields=None,key=None):
    if fields is None: fields=MAIN_FIELDS
    if key is None:key='PERCENT_CPU'
    return dict(name=name, fields=fields[:],sort_key=key,tree_sort_key='PID',
        tree_view_always_by_pid=0,tree_view=0,sort_direction=sort_direction(key),
        tree_sort_direction=1,all_branches_collapsed=0)


class Settings:
    def __init__(self,opts):
        self.values=DEFAULTS.copy()
        self.screens=[new_screen(),new_screen('I/O',IO_FIELDS,'IO_RATE')]
        self.layout='two_50_50'
        n=os.cpu_count() or 1
        suffix='8' if n>32 else '4' if n>16 else '2' if n>8 else ''
        if n>4:
            self.meters=[[('LeftCPUs'+suffix,1),('Memory',1),('Swap',1)], [('RightCPUs'+suffix,1),('Tasks',2),('LoadAverage',2),('Uptime',2)]]
        else:
            self.meters=[[('AllCPUs',1),('Memory',1),('Swap',1)],[('Tasks',2),('LoadAverage',2),('Uptime',2)]]
        self.path=self.config_path()
        self.changed=False
        self.read()
        for k in ['delay','enable_mouse','highlight_changes','highlight_changes_delay_secs','hide_function_bar']:
            if k in opts:
                if self.values[k]!=opts[k]:self.changed=True
                self.values[k]=opts[k]
        s=self.screens[0]
        if 'sort' in opts:
            if opts.get('tree'):
                s['tree_sort_key']=opts['sort'];s['tree_sort_direction']=sort_direction(opts['sort'])

                s['sort_key']=opts['sort'];s['sort_direction']=sort_direction(opts['sort']);s['tree_view']=0

def memory_size(kb):
    if kb<100000:return str(int(kb))
    v=kb/1024
    if v<1000:return f'{v:.0f}M'
    v/=1024
    if v<100:return f'{v:.2f}G'
    if v<1000:return f'{v:.1f}G'
    v/=1024
    return f'{v:.2f}T'


def meter_size(kb):
    if kb<1024:return f'{kb:.0f}K'
    v=kb/1024
    unit='M'
    if v>=1024:v/=1024;unit='G'
    if v>=1024:v/=1024;unit='T'
    return (f'{v:.1f}' if v<100 else f'{v:.0f}')+unit


def time_value(ticks,clock=100):
    seconds=ticks/clock
    if seconds<3600:return f'{int(seconds//60)}:{int(seconds%60):02d}.{int(ticks%clock)*100//clock:02d}'
    if seconds<360000:return f'{int(seconds//3600)}h{int(seconds//60%60):02d}:{int(seconds%60):02d}'
    return f'{int(seconds//86400)}d{int(seconds//3600%24):02d}h'


def rate_value(n):
    units=['B/s','K/s','M/s','G/s','T/s'];idx=0
    while n>=1024 and idx<4:n/=1024;idx+=1
    return f'{n:.2f} {units[idx]}'

def atoi(s, default=0):
    m=re.match(r'\s*([+-]?\d+)',str(s))
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else default


def sort_direction(col):

class Settings:
    def __init__(self,opts):
        self.values=DEFAULTS.copy()
        self.screens=[new_screen(),new_screen('I/O',IO_FIELDS,'IO_RATE')]
        self.layout='two_50_50'
        n=os.cpu_count() or 1
        suffix='8' if n>32 else '4' if n>16 else '2' if n>8 else ''
        if n>4:
            self.meters=[[('LeftCPUs'+suffix,1),('Memory',1),('Swap',1)], [('RightCPUs'+suffix,1),('Tasks',2),('LoadAverage',2),('Uptime',2)]]
        else:
            self.meters=[[('AllCPUs',1),('Memory',1),('Swap',1)],[('Tasks',2),('LoadAverage',2),('Uptime',2)]]
        self.path=self.config_path()
        self.changed=False
        self.read()
        for k in ['delay','enable_mouse','highlight_changes','highlight_changes_delay_secs','hide_function_bar']:
            if k in opts:
                if self.values[k]!=opts[k]:self.changed=True
                self.values[k]=opts[k]
        s=self.screens[0]
        if 'sort' in opts:
            if opts.get('tree'):
                s['tree_sort_key']=opts['sort'];s['tree_sort_direction']=sort_direction(opts['sort'])
            else:
                s['sort_key']=opts['sort'];s['sort_direction']=sort_direction(opts['sort']);s['tree_view']=0
            self.changed=True
        if opts.get('tree'):
            s['tree_view']=1;self.changed=True

    def config_path(self):
        if 'HTOPRC' in os.environ:return os.environ['HTOPRC']
        home=os.environ.get('HOME') or pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir
        self.legacy=os.path.join(home,'.htoprc')
        return os.path.join(os.environ.get('XDG_CONFIG_HOME') or os.path.join(home,'.config'),'htop','htoprc')

    def read(self):
        path=self.path
        try: text=pathlib.Path(path).read_text(errors='replace')
        except OSError:
            try:text=pathlib.Path(getattr(self,'legacy','/nonexistent')).read_text(errors='replace')
            except OSError:
                self.changed=True;return
            self.changed=True
        valid=False; named=False; current=None
        pending_meters={};pending_modes={}
        for line in text.splitlines():
            if not line or line.startswith('#') or '=' not in line:continue
            k,v=line.split('=',1);k=k.strip();v=v.strip()
            if k=='htop_version':continue
            if k=='config_reader_min_version':
                valid=True;n=atoi(v)
                if n>3:
                    sys.stderr.write(f'WARNING: {path} specifies configuration format\n         version v{n}, but this htop binary only supports up to version v3.\n         The configuration file will be downgraded to v3 when htop exits.\n')
                    self.changed=True
            elif k in self.values:
                self.values[k]=atoi(v);valid=True
            elif k=='header_layout':
                if v in [l[0] for l in LAYOUTS]:self.layout=v
                valid=True
            elif k.startswith('screen:'):
                if not named:self.screens=[];named=True
                fs=[x for x in v.split() if x in COL_ID]
                current=new_screen(k[7:],fs or MAIN_FIELDS)
                self.screens.append(current);valid=True
            elif k.startswith('.') and current is not None:
                sub=k[1:]
                if sub in ('sort_key','tree_sort_key') and v in COL_ID:current[sub]=v
                elif sub in current:current[sub]=atoi(v)
            elif k=='fields' and not named:
                fs=[ID_COL[n] for n in [atoi(x,-1) for x in v.split()] if n in ID_COL]
                if fs:self.screens[0]['fields']=fs
                valid=True
            elif k in self.screens[0]:
                if k in ('sort_key','tree_sort_key'):self.screens[0][k]=ID_COL.get(atoi(v),'PID')
                else:self.screens[0][k]=atoi(v)
                valid=True
            elif k.startswith('column_meters_') or k in ('left_meters','right_meters'):
                n=0 if k=='left_meters' else 1 if k=='right_meters' else atoi(k[len('column_meters_'):])
                pending_meters[n]=v.split();valid=True
            elif k.startswith('column_meter_modes_') or k in ('left_meter_modes','right_meter_modes'):
                n=0 if k=='left_meter_modes' else 1 if k=='right_meter_modes' else atoi(k[len('column_meter_modes_'):])
                pending_modes[n]=[atoi(s,1) for s in v.split()];valid=True
        if pending_meters:
            count=max(len(self.layout_widths()),max(pending_meters)+1)
            self.meters=[[] for _ in range(count)]
            for n,ms in pending_meters.items():
                for i,m in enumerate(ms):
                    if m not in METER_INFO:continue
                    modes=pending_modes.get(n,[])
                    mode=modes[i] if i<len(modes) and 1<=modes[i]<=4 else METER_INFO[m][3]
                    self.meters[n].append((m,mode))
        if not valid:self.changed=True
        self.values['delay']=max(1,min(255,self.values['delay']))
        self.values['color_scheme']=max(0,min(7,self.values['color_scheme']))
        self.values['hide_function_bar']=max(0,min(2,self.values['hide_function_bar']))
        if not self.screens:self.screens=[new_screen()]
        while len(self.meters)<len(self.layout_widths()):self.meters.append([])

    def layout_widths(self):
        return next((l[2] for l in LAYOUTS if l[0]==self.layout),[50,50])

    def save(self):
        if not self.changed:return
        s=self.screens[0]
        out=['# Beware! This file is rewritten by htop when settings are changed in the interface.',
             '# The parser is also very primitive, and not human-friendly.',
             'htop_version='+VERSION,'config_reader_min_version=3',
             'fields='+' '.join(str(COL_ID[c]) for c in s['fields'])]
        out += [f'{k}={v}' for k,v in self.values.items()]
        out += ['header_layout='+self.layout]
        for i,ms in enumerate(self.meters[:len(self.layout_widths())]):
            out.append(f'column_meters_{i}='+' '.join(m for m,mode in ms))
            out.append(f'column_meter_modes_{i}='+' '.join(str(mode) for m,mode in ms))
        for key in ['tree_view','sort_key','tree_sort_key','sort_direction','tree_sort_direction','tree_view_always_by_pid','all_branches_collapsed']:
            val=s[key]
            if key in ('sort_key','tree_sort_key'):val=COL_ID.get(val,0)
            out.append(f'{key}={val}')
        for s in self.screens:
            out.append(f'screen:{s["name"]}='+' '.join(s['fields']))
            for key in ['sort_key','tree_sort_key','tree_view_always_by_pid','tree_view','sort_direction','tree_sort_direction','all_branches_collapsed']:
                out.append(f'.{key}={s[key]}')
        try:
            p=pathlib.Path(self.path)
            p.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
            p.write_text('\n'.join(out)+'\n')
        except OSError:pass


def textfile(path,default=''):
    try:return pathlib.Path(path).read_text(errors='replace')
    except OSError:return default


def clean(s):
    return ''.join(c if c.isprintable() else '?' for c in s)


class Sampler:
    def __init__(self):
        self.ncpu=os.cpu_count() or 1
        self.clock=os.sysconf('SC_CLK_TCK')
        self.pagesize=os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE')//1024
        self.previous={}
        self.previous_cpu=[]
        self.cpus=[(0.,0.,0.,0.)]*(self.ncpu+1)
        self.last_time=0
        self.processes=[]
        self.mem={}
        self.load=(0,0,0)
        self.uptime=0
        self.hostname=socket.gethostname()
        self.uid_names={}
        self.running=0
        self.total=0
        self.threads=0
        self.kt=0
        self.disk_prev=None
        self.net_prev=None
        self.disk_rates=(0,0)
        self.net_rates=(0,0)
        self.update()

    def update(self):
        now=time.monotonic()
        elapsed=now-self.last_time if self.last_time else 0
        self.uptime=float(textfile('/proc/uptime','0 0').split()[0])
        self.boot=time.time()-self.uptime
        self.load=os.getloadavg()
        self.mem={k:atoi(v) for k,v in (line.split(':',1) for line in textfile('/proc/meminfo').splitlines() if ':' in line)}
        cpu_lines=[]
        for line in textfile('/proc/stat').splitlines():
            if line.startswith('cpu'):
                nums=list(map(int,line.split()[1:]));cpu_lines.append(nums)
            elif line.startswith('procs_running '): self.running=atoi(line.split()[1])
        cpus=[]
        for i,ns in enumerate(cpu_lines):
            old=self.previous_cpu[i] if i<len(self.previous_cpu) else ns
            ds=[a-b for a,b in zip(ns,old)]
            total=sum(ds[:8]) or 1
            cpus.append(((ds[0]+ds[1])*100/total, (ds[2]+sum(ds[5:7]))*100/total,
                ds[1]*100/total, (sum(ds[8:10]) if len(ds)>8 else 0)*100/total))
        self.cpus=cpus;self.previous_cpu=cpu_lines
        processes=[];prev={};nt=0;kt=0
        for ent in os.listdir('/proc'):
            if not ent.isdigit():continue
            pid=int(ent)
            p=self.read_process(pid,pid,now,elapsed)
            if not p:continue
            processes.append(p);prev[pid]=p
            if p['kernel']:kt+=1
            try:ts=os.listdir(f'/proc/{pid}/task')
            except OSError:ts=[]
            for tid in ts:
                if not tid.isdigit() or int(tid)==pid:continue
                t=self.read_process(int(tid),pid,now,elapsed,p)
                if t:processes.append(t);prev[int(tid)]=t;nt+=1
        self.previous=prev;self.processes=processes
        self.total=len(processes)-nt;self.threads=nt;self.kt=kt
        self.last_time=now
        io=[0,0]
        for line in textfile('/proc/diskstats').splitlines():
            f=line.split()
            if len(f)>10 and (f[2].startswith('sd') and not f[2][-1].isdigit() or re.fullmatch(r'nvme\d+n\d+',f[2]) or f[2].startswith('vd') and not f[2][-1].isdigit()):
                io[0]+=int(f[5])*512;io[1]+=int(f[9])*512
        if elapsed and self.disk_prev:self.disk_rates=tuple(max(0,(a-b)/elapsed) for a,b in zip(io,self.disk_prev))
        self.disk_prev=io
        net=[0,0]
        for line in textfile('/proc/net/dev').splitlines():
            if ':' not in line:continue
            dev,vals=line.split(':');f=vals.split()
            if dev.strip()=='lo':continue
            net[0]+=int(f[0]);net[1]+=int(f[8])
        if elapsed and self.net_prev:self.net_rates=tuple(max(0,(a-b)/elapsed) for a,b in zip(net,self.net_prev))
        self.net_prev=net

    def read_process(self,pid,tgid,now,elapsed,parent=None):
        path=f'/proc/{tgid}' if pid==tgid else f'/proc/{tgid}/task/{pid}'
        try:
            stat=pathlib.Path(path+'/stat').read_text()
            start=stat.index('(');end=stat.rindex(')')
            comm=stat[start+1:end];f=stat[end+2:].split()
            vals={}
            vals['PID']=pid;vals['TGID']=tgid;vals['STATE']=f[0];vals['PPID']=int(f[1]);vals['PGRP']=int(f[2]);vals['SESSION']=int(f[3]);vals['tty']=int(f[4]);vals['TPGID']=int(f[5]);
            for name,idx in [('MINFLT',7),('CMINFLT',8),('MAJFLT',9),('CMAJFLT',10),('UTIME',11),('STIME',12),('CUTIME',13),('CSTIME',14),('PRIORITY',15),('NICE',16),('NLWP',17),('start',19),('PROCESSOR',36)]:
                vals[name]=int(f[idx]) if idx<len(f) else 0
            vals['TIME']=vals['UTIME']+vals['STIME'];vals['start']=vals['start']/self.clock
            vals['ELAPSED']=self.uptime-vals['start']
            vals['STARTTIME']=self.boot+vals['start']
            vals['M_VIRT']=int(f[20])//1024;vals['M_RESIDENT']=int(f[21])*self.pagesize
            mems=list(map(int,pathlib.Path(path+'/statm').read_text().split()))
            vals['M_SHARE']=mems[2]*self.pagesize;vals['M_TRS']=mems[3]*self.pagesize;vals['M_DRS']=mems[5]*self.pagesize
            vals['M_PRIV']=max(0,vals['M_RESIDENT']-vals['M_SHARE']);vals['M_LRS']=0
            uid=os.stat(path).st_uid;vals['ST_UID']=uid
            if uid not in self.uid_names:
                try:self.uid_names[uid]=pwd.getpwuid(uid).pw_name
                except KeyError:self.uid_names[uid]=str(uid)
            vals['USER']=self.uid_names[uid]
            cmd=pathlib.Path(path+'/cmdline').read_bytes().rstrip(b'\0').replace(b'\0',b' ').decode(errors='replace')
            vals['rawcmd']=cmd or comm;vals['Command']=clean(cmd or comm)
            vals['COMM']=comm;vals['kernel']=not cmd and vals['STATE']!='Z'
            try:exe=os.readlink(path+'/exe')
            except OSError:exe=''
            vals['exe_path']=exe;vals['EXE']=os.path.basename(exe)
            try:vals['CWD']=os.readlink(path+'/cwd')
            except OSError:vals['CWD']='-'
            vals['thread']=pid!=tgid
            vals['PERCENT_MEM']=100*vals['M_RESIDENT']/(self.mem.get('MemTotal') or 1)
            previous=self.previous.get(pid)
            vals['PERCENT_CPU']=max(0,(vals['TIME']-previous['TIME'])/self.clock/elapsed*100) if elapsed and previous else 0.
            vals['PERCENT_NORM_CPU']=vals['PERCENT_CPU']/self.ncpu
            vals['OOM']=atoi(textfile(path+'/oom_score'))
            vals['SECATTR']=textfile(path+'/attr/current','-').strip() or '-'
            cgroup=textfile(path+'/cgroup').splitlines()
            vals['CGROUP']=cgroup[0].split(':',2)[-1] if cgroup else '-';vals['CCGROUP']=vals['CGROUP']
            vals['CONTAINER']='-';vals['ISCONTAINER']=0
            group=textfile(path+'/autogroup')
            mm=re.search(r'autogroup-(\d+) nice (-?\d+)',group)
            vals['AUTOGROUP_ID']=int(mm[1]) if mm else -1;vals['AUTOGROUP_NICE']=int(mm[2]) if mm else 0
            vals['SCHEDULERPOLICY']=int(f[38]) if len(f)>38 else 0
            io={k:atoi(v) for k,v in (l.split(':',1) for l in textfile(path+'/io').splitlines() if ':' in l)}
            for k,key in [('RCHAR','rchar'),('WCHAR','wchar'),('SYSCR','syscr'),('SYSCW','syscw'),('RBYTES','read_bytes'),('WBYTES','write_bytes'),('CNCLWB','cancelled_write_bytes')]:vals[k]=io.get(key,0)
            vals['IO_READ_RATE']=max(0,(vals['RBYTES']-previous['RBYTES'])/elapsed) if elapsed and previous else 0
            vals['IO_WRITE_RATE']=max(0,(vals['WBYTES']-previous['WBYTES'])/elapsed) if elapsed and previous else 0
            vals['IO_RATE']=vals['IO_READ_RATE']+vals['IO_WRITE_RATE']
            vals['IO_PRIORITY']='B'+str((vals['NICE']+20)//5)
            status={k:v.strip() for k,v in (l.split(':',1) for l in textfile(path+'/status').splitlines() if ':' in l)}
            vals['M_SWAP']=atoi(status.get('VmSwap',0));vals['M_PSS']=0;vals['M_PSSWP']=0
            ctx=atoi(status.get('voluntary_ctxt_switches',0))+atoi(status.get('nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches',0))
            vals['ctx']=ctx;vals['CTXT']=max(0,ctx-previous['ctx']) if previous else 0
            vals['GPU_TIME']=0;vals['GPU_PERCENT']=0
            vals['seen']=previous.get('seen',now) if previous else now
            tty=vals['tty'];vals['TTY']=f'pts/{tty & 255}' if (tty>>8)&255 in (136,137,138,139,140,141,142,143) else '?' if tty==0 else f'{(tty>>8)&255}:{tty&255}'
            return vals
        except (OSError,ValueError,IndexError,ProcessLookupError):return None


def memory_size(kb):
    if kb<100000:return str(int(kb))
    v=kb/1024
    if v<1000:return f'{v:.0f}M'
    v/=1024
    if v<100:return f'{v:.2f}G'
    if v<1000:return f'{v:.1f}G'
    v/=1024
    return f'{v:.2f}T'


def meter_size(kb):
    if kb<1024:return f'{kb:.0f}K'
    v=kb/1024
    unit='M'
    if v>=1024:v/=1024;unit='G'
    if v>=1024:v/=1024;unit='T'
    return (f'{v:.1f}' if v<100 else f'{v:.0f}')+unit


def time_value(ticks,clock=100):
    seconds=ticks/clock
    if seconds<3600:return f'{int(seconds//60)}:{int(seconds%60):02d}.{int(ticks%clock)*100//clock:02d}'
    if seconds<360000:return f'{int(seconds//3600)}h{int(seconds//60%60):02d}:{int(seconds%60):02d}'
    return f'{int(seconds//86400)}d{int(seconds//3600%24):02d}h'


def rate_value(n):
    units=['B/s','K/s','M/s','G/s','T/s'];idx=0
    while n>=1024 and idx<4:n/=1024;idx+=1
    return f'{n:.2f} {units[idx]}'

        elif col in ('COMM','EXE','CWD','CGROUP','CCGROUP','CONTAINER','SECATTR','TTY'):return str(v)[:width-1].ljust(width-1)+' '
        elif col=='SCHEDULERPOLICY':val={0:'OTHER',1:'FIFO',2:'RR',3:'BATCH',5:'IDLE',6:'DEADL'}.get(v,'-')
        elif col=='ISCONTAINER':val='yes' if v else 'no'
        elif col=='PRIORITY':val='RT' if v<0 else str(v)
        elif col=='AUTOGROUP_ID':val=str(v) if v>=0 else '-'
        else:val=str(v)
        return val.rjust(width-1)+' '

    def table(self,y,x=0,focused=True):
        width=self.w-x
        key=self.s['tree_sort_key'] if self.s['tree_view'] else self.s['sort_key']
        direction=self.s['tree_sort_direction'] if self.s['tree_view'] else self.s['sort_direction']
        self.put(y,x,'','header',width)
        xx=-self.hscroll
        self.table_columns=[]
        for f in self.s['fields']:
            head,w=HEADINGS.get(f,(f+' ',len(f)+1));attr='select' if f==key else 'header'
            if f==key and head.endswith(' '):head=head[:-1]+('+' if direction==1 else '-')
            self.put(y,x+max(0,xx),head[max(0,-xx):],attr)
            self.table_columns.append((x+xx,x+xx+(w or max(1,width-xx)),f))
            xx+=w or len(head)
        bottom=self.h-1 if self.has_footer() else self.h
        count=max(0,bottom-y-1);self.table_height=count;self.body_y=y
        self.scroll=max(0,min(self.scroll,max(0,len(self.visible)-count)))
        if self.sel<self.scroll:self.scroll=self.sel
        if self.sel>=self.scroll+count:self.scroll=max(0,self.sel-count+1)
        for row,p in enumerate(self.visible[self.scroll:self.scroll+count]):
            selected=self.scroll+row==self.sel
            highlight='select' if focused else 'unfocus'
            if selected:self.put(y+row+1,x,'',highlight,width)
            xx=-self.hscroll
            for f in self.s['fields']:
                txt=self.cell(p,f)
                role='normal'
                if selected:role=highlight
                elif p['PID'] in self.tagged:role='tag'
                elif self.v['shadow_other_users'] and p['ST_UID']!=os.getuid():role='dim'
                elif self.v['highlight_changes'] and time.monotonic()-p['seen']<self.v['highlight_changes_delay_secs']:role='green'
                elif f=='Command':
                    if p['thread'] and self.v['highlight_threads']:role='green'
                    elif p['kernel']:role='dim'
                elif f=='USER' and p['ST_UID']!=os.getuid():role='dim'
                elif f=='STATE':role='green' if p['STATE']=='R' else 'red' if p['STATE'] in ('D','Z') else 'dim'
                elif f=='NICE':role='blue' if p[f]>0 else 'red' if p[f]<0 else 'dim'
                elif f in ('PERCENT_CPU','PERCENT_MEM','TIME') and not p.get(f):role='dim'
                self.put(y+row+1,x+max(0,xx),txt[max(0,-xx):],role)
                if not selected and p['PID'] not in self.tagged:
                    if f.startswith('M_') and self.v['highlight_megabytes'] and p.get(f,0)>=1000:
                        n=max(1,len(txt.rstrip())-3);self.put(y+row+1,x+max(0,xx),txt[:n][max(0,-xx):],'cyan')
                    elif f=='Command' and self.v['highlight_base_name']:
                        command=self.command(p);first=command.split(' ',1)[0];pos=first.rfind('/')+1
                        start=xx+len(self.prefix.get(p['PID'],''))+pos
                        self.put(y+row+1,x+max(0,start),first[pos:][max(0,-start):],'bold')
                xx+=len(txt)

    def has_footer(self):
        return self.mode!='main' or self.prompt is not None or not (self.v['hide_function_bar']==2 or self.hide_bar)

    def meter_height(self,m,style):
        if 'CPUs' in m:
            count=self.sample.ncpu if m.startswith('All') else (self.sample.ncpu+1)//2 if m.startswith('Left') else self.sample.ncpu//2
            match=re.search(r'CPUs(\d+)$',m);columns=int(match[1]) if match else 1
            return max(1,math.ceil(count/columns))*(3 if style in (3,4) else 1)
        return 3 if style in (3,4) else 1

    def header(self):
        if self.no_meters:return 0
        margin=bool(self.v['header_margin']);x=2 if margin else 0;y=1 if margin else 0
        available=self.w-(4 if margin else 0);maxheight=0
        widths=self.settings.layout_widths()
        for i,percent in enumerate(widths):
            rawwidth=available*percent//100
            if i==len(widths)-1:rawwidth=self.w-(2 if margin else 0)-x
            width=rawwidth-(2 if i<len(widths)-1 else 0)
            my=y
            for m,style in self.settings.meters[i] if i<len(self.settings.meters) else []:
                self.draw_meter(my,x,max(1,width),m,style)
                my+=self.meter_height(m,style)
            maxheight=max(maxheight,my-y);x+=rawwidth
        body=y+maxheight+(1 if margin else 0)
        if self.v['screen_tabs']:
            x=2
            names=['Setup'] if self.mode=='setup' else [s['name'] for s in self.settings.screens]
            for i,name in enumerate(names):
                text='['+name+']'
                self.put(body,x,text,'header' if self.mode=='setup' or i==self.tab else 'dim')
                x+=len(text)+1
            body+=1
        return body

    def bar_meter(self,y,x,width,label,value,parts):
        self.put(y,x,label,'label');size=width-len(label)
        if size<=0:return
        if size==1:self.put(y,x+len(label),']','bold');return
        inner=max(0,size-2);xx=x+len(label)
        self.put(y,xx,'['+' '*inner+']','bold')
        pos=0
        for amount,role,char in parts:
            count=max(0,min(inner-pos,int(math.ceil(amount*inner))))
            self.put(y,xx+1+pos,char*count,role);pos+=count
        if value:
            if len(value)>inner:value=value[:inner]
            self.put(y,xx+1+inner-len(value),value,'brightdim')

    def cpu_meter(self,y,x,width,num,style=1):
        index=num+1
        vals=self.sample.cpus[index] if index<len(self.sample.cpus) else (0,0,0,0)
        user,kernel,nice,guest=vals
        percent=min(100,max(0,user+kernel+(guest if self.v['account_guest_in_cpu_meter'] else 0)))
        label='CPU' if num<0 else f'{num+(1 if self.v["cpu_count_from_one"] else 0):3d}'
        value=f'{percent:.1f}%' if percent<100 else '100.0%'
        if self.v['show_cpu_frequency']:value+=' '+str(int(self.cpu_frequency(num)))+'MHz'
        if style==2:self.put(y,x,label+' '+value,'label')
        elif style==3:self.graph(y,x,width,label,percent)
        elif style==4:self.led(y,x,width,label,value)
        else:self.bar_meter(y,x,width,label,value if self.v['show_cpu_usage'] else '',[(nice/100,'blue','|'),((user-nice)/100,'green','|'),(kernel/100,'red','|'),(guest/100,'cyan','|')])

    def cpu_frequency(self,num):
        val=textfile(f'/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu{max(0,num)}/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq')
        return atoi(val)/1000 if val else 0

    def graph(self,y,x,width,label,percent):
        self.put(y,x,label,'label')
        # The history begins empty; a new value is appended at the right edge.
        for row in range(3):
            if percent>=(2-row)*100/3:self.put(y+row,x+max(0,width-1),'.' if not self.unicode else '⣀','green')

    def led(self,y,x,width,label,value):
        self.put(y,x,label,'label')
        # Compact three-line seven-segment glyphs.
        glyphs={'0':[' _ ','| |','|_|'],'1':['   ','  |','  |'],'2':[' _ ',' _|','|_ '],'3':[' _ ',' _|',' _|'],'4':['   ','|_|','  |'],'5':[' _ ','|_ ',' _|'],'6':[' _ ','|_ ','|_|'],'7':[' _ ','  |','  |'],'8':[' _ ','|_|','|_|'],'9':[' _ ','|_|',' _|'],':':[' ','o','o'],'.':[' ',' ','o'],'%':['o /',' / ','/ o']}
        xx=x+len(label)+1
        for ch in value:
            g=glyphs.get(ch,[ch,' ',' '])
            for row,txt in enumerate(g):self.put(y+row,xx,txt,'green')
            xx+=len(g[0])+1
            if xx>=x+width:break

    def draw_meter(self,y,x,width,m,style):
        if 'CPUs' in m:
            n=self.sample.ncpu
            begin=0 if not m.startswith('Right') else (n+1)//2
            count=n if m.startswith('All') else (n+1)//2 if m.startswith('Left') else n//2
            mo=re.search(r'CPUs(\d+)$',m);columns=int(mo[1]) if mo else 1
            rows=max(1,math.ceil(count/columns));unit=max(1,width//columns);extra=width+1-unit*columns
            for col in range(columns):
                for row in range(rows):
                    idx=col*rows+row
                    if idx<count:self.cpu_meter(y+row*(3 if style in (3,4) else 1),x+col*unit+min(col,max(0,extra)),unit,begin+idx,style)
            return
        if m.startswith('CPU('):self.cpu_meter(y,x,width,atoi(m[4:])-1,style);return
        if m=='CPU':self.cpu_meter(y,x,width,-1,style);return
        mem=self.sample.mem;total=mem.get('MemTotal',1);swap=mem.get('SwapTotal',0)
        cached=max(0,mem.get('Cached',0)+mem.get('SReclaimable',0)-mem.get('Shmem',0));buffers=mem.get('Buffers',0);shared=mem.get('Shmem',0)
        used=max(0,total-mem.get('MemFree',0)-buffers-cached)
        swapused=swap-mem.get('SwapFree',0)
        label='';value='';parts=[];pct=0
        if m in ('Memory','MemorySwap'):
            label='Mem';value=meter_size(used)+'/'+meter_size(total)
            parts=[(max(0,used-shared)/total,'green','|'),(shared/total,'magenta','|'),(buffers/total,'blue','|'),(cached/total if self.v['show_cached_memory'] else 0,'yellow','|')];pct=used/total*100
        elif m=='Swap':
            label='Swp';value=meter_size(swapused)+'/'+meter_size(swap);parts=[(swapused/(swap or 1),'red','|'),(mem.get('SwapCached',0)/(swap or 1),'yellow','|')];pct=swapused/(swap or 1)*100
        elif m=='HugePages':
            label='Huge';hugetotal=mem.get('HugePages_Total',0)*mem.get('Hugepagesize',0);hugeused=hugetotal-mem.get('HugePages_Free',0)*mem.get('Hugepagesize',0);value=meter_size(hugeused)+'/'+meter_size(hugetotal);parts=[(hugeused/(hugetotal or 1),'green','|')]
        elif m=='Tasks':
            label='Tasks: ';value=f'{self.sample.total}, {self.sample.threads} thr, {self.sample.kt} kthr; {self.sample.running} running'
        elif m in ('LoadAverage','Load'):
            label='Load average: ' if m=='LoadAverage' else 'Load: '
            value=' '.join(f'{x:.2f}' for x in (self.sample.load if m=='LoadAverage' else self.sample.load[:1]));pct=self.sample.load[0]/self.sample.ncpu*100
        elif m=='Uptime':
            label='Uptime: ';seconds=int(self.sample.uptime);days=seconds//86400
            value=(f'{days} day'+('s' if days!=1 else '')+', ' if days else '')+f'{seconds//3600%24:02d}:{seconds//60%60:02d}:{seconds%60:02d}'
        elif m=='UptimeSeconds':label='Uptime: ';value=str(int(self.sample.uptime))
        elif m=='Clock':label='Time: ';value=time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')
        elif m=='Date':label='Date: ';value=time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        elif m=='DateTime':label='Date and Time: ';value=time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        elif m=='Hostname':label='Hostname: ';value=self.sample.hostname
        elif m=='System':label='System: ';value=' '.join(os.uname()[i] for i in (0,2,4))
        elif m=='Battery':label='Battery: ';value='N/A'
        elif m in ('DiskIO','DiskIORate','DiskIOTime'):
            label='Disk IO: ';value=' '.join((rate_value(self.sample.disk_rates[0]),'read,',rate_value(self.sample.disk_rates[1]),'write'))
        elif m=='NetworkIO':label='Network: ';value=rate_value(self.sample.net_rates[0])+' rx, '+rate_value(self.sample.net_rates[1])+' tx'
        elif m=='FileDescriptors':
            fs=textfile('/proc/sys/fs/file-nr','0 0 0').split();label='FDs: ';value=fs[0]+'/'+fs[2] if len(fs)>2 else 'N/A'
        elif m=='SELinux':label='SELinux: ';value='disabled'
        elif m.startswith('Systemd'):label='Systemd: ';value='N/A'
        elif m.startswith('OpenRC'):label='OpenRC: ';value='N/A'
        elif m.startswith('PressureStall'):
            typ='cpu' if 'CPU' in m else 'io' if 'IO' in m else 'irq' if 'IRQ' in m else 'memory';kind='full' if m.endswith('Full') else 'some'
            nums=textfile('/proc/pressure/'+typ)
            entry=next((l for l in nums.splitlines() if l.startswith(kind+' ')),None)
            label='PSI '+kind+' '+typ+': '
            value=' '.join(f'{float(v):.2f}' for v in re.findall(r'avg\d+=(\S+)',entry)) if entry else 'N/A'
        elif m=='Blank':return
        else:label=METER_INFO.get(m,(m,m))[1]+': ';value='N/A'
        if style==1:
            self.bar_meter(y,x,width,label.rstrip(': '),value,parts)
        elif style==3:self.graph(y,x,width,label.rstrip(': '),pct)
        elif style==4:self.led(y,x,width,label.rstrip(': '),value)
        else:
            self.put(y,x,label,'normal');self.put(y,x+len(label),value,'bold' if m in ('Tasks','LoadAverage','Uptime','Clock') else 'normal')

    def help_screen(self):
        lines=resource('interactive_help.txt').splitlines()
        for y,line in enumerate(lines):
            role='title' if y<2 or line=='Press any key to return.' else 'normal'
            self.raw(y,0,line,role)
            if 11<=y<=29:
                # Color each key legend, leaving the descriptions untouched.
                for m in re.finditer(r'\S[^:]*?: ',line):
                    if m.start()>55:continue
                if ': ' in line:
                    end=line.index(': ')+2;self.raw(y,0,line[:end],'title')
                    m=re.search(r' {2,}(\S[^:]*?: )',line[end:])
                    if m:self.raw(y,end+m.start(1),m[1],'title')
            elif y in (3,4,5):
                for word,role2 in [('low','blue'),('normal','green'),('kernel','red'),('guest','cyan'),('used','green' if y==4 else 'red'),('shared','magenta'),('compressed','brightdim'),('buffers','blue'),('cache','yellow'),('frontswap','brightdim')]:
                    start=line.find(word)
                    if start>=0:self.raw(y,start,word,role2)
                st=line.find('[')
                if st>=0:self.raw(y,st,'[','bold');self.raw(y,len(line)-1,']','bold')
                m=re.search(r'used[%/]',line[40:])
                if m:
                    start=40+m.start();self.raw(y,start,line[start:-1],'brightdim')
            elif y==9:
                for st,role2 in [('R:','green'),('S:','brightdim'),('t:','green'),('Z:','red'),('D:','red')]:
                    ix=line.find(st)
                    if ix>=0:self.raw(y,ix,st[0],role2)

"""Black-box regression tests. Run after ./compile.sh with unittest discovery."""
import os
import pathlib
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
PROGRAM=ROOT/'executable'

class CommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.home=tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.env={**os.environ,'HOME':self.home.name,'HTOPRC':str(pathlib.Path(self.home.name)/'htoprc'),'TERM':'unknown'}
    def tearDown(self):self.home.cleanup()
    def run_program(self,*args,term=None):
        env=self.env.copy()
        if term:env['TERM']=term
        return subprocess.run([str(PROGRAM),*args],input=b'',capture_output=True,env=env,timeout=5)
    def test_version(self):
        p=self.run_program('--version')
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,b'htop 3.5.0-dev-76f3fce\n',b''))
    def test_help(self):
        p=self.run_program('--help')
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,(ROOT/'src'/'cli_help.txt').read_bytes())
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
    def test_columns(self):
        p=self.run_program('--sort-key=help')
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,(ROOT/'src'/'columns.txt').read_bytes())
    def test_argument_errors(self):
        for args,error in [(['-d','bad'],'invalid delay value "bad".'),
                           (['-s','pid'],'invalid column "pid".'),
                           (['--user=not-a-valid-user-123'],'invalid user "not-a-valid-user-123".'),
                           (['-n','0'],'maximum iteration count must be positive.'),
                           (['-n','none'],'invalid maximum iteration count "none".'),
                           (['--highlight-changes=oops'],'invalid highlight delay value "oops".')]:
            with self.subTest(args=args):
                p=self.run_program(*args)
                self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
                self.assertEqual(p.stderr,('Error: '+error+'\n').encode())
                self.assertFalse(p.stdout)
    def test_help_short_circuits(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_program('unused','--version','--bad').returncode,0)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_program('--bad','--version').returncode,1)
    def test_missing_terminal(self):
        p=self.run_program()
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,b'Error opening terminal: unknown.\n')
    def test_numeric_prefix_is_accepted(self):
        p=self.run_program('-d','2.5')
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,b'Error opening terminal: unknown.\n')
    def test_dumb_snapshot(self):
        p=self.run_program('--no-meters','-n','1',term='dumb')
        header='  PID USER       PRI  NI  VIRT   RES   SHR S  CPU%-MEM%   TIME+  Command'
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,(' '*1920+header.ljust(80)+'\r\r').encode())
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        text=pathlib.Path(self.env['HTOPRC']).read_text()
        self.assertIn('screen:Main=PID USER PRIORITY NICE',text)
        self.assertIn('column_meters_0=',text)
    def test_cli_overrides_do_not_rewrite_existing_config(self):
        path=pathlib.Path(self.env['HTOPRC'])
        original='fields=0 1\ndelay=15\n'
        path.write_text(original)
        p=self.run_program('-d','2','--no-meters','-n','1',term='dumb')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        self.assertEqual(path.read_text(),original)

if __name__=='__main__':unittest.main()

"""Exercise keyboard-driven screens and process actions through a real PTY."""
import fcntl
import os
import pathlib
import pty
import select
import struct
import subprocess
import tempfile
import termios
import time
import unittest

ROOT=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

class TerminalTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.directory=tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.rc=pathlib.Path(self.directory.name)/'htoprc'
        self.child=subprocess.Popen(['sleep','30'])
        self.master,self.slave=pty.openpty()
        fcntl.ioctl(self.slave,termios.TIOCSWINSZ,struct.pack('HHHH',35,100,0,0))
        self.process=subprocess.Popen([str(ROOT/'executable'),'--no-meters','-p',str(self.child.pid),'-d','1'],
            stdin=self.slave,stdout=self.slave,stderr=self.slave,
            env={**os.environ,'TERM':'xterm-256color','HTOPRC':str(self.rc)})
        os.close(self.slave)
        self.read(.3)
    def tearDown(self):
        if self.process.poll() is None:self.process.terminate()
        self.process.wait(timeout=3)
        if self.child.poll() is None:self.child.terminate()
        self.child.wait(timeout=3)
        os.close(self.master)
        self.directory.cleanup()
    def read(self,seconds=.2):
        end=time.monotonic()+seconds
        data=b''
        while time.monotonic()<end:
            remaining=end-time.monotonic()
            if select.select([self.master],[],[],max(0,remaining))[0]:
                try:chunk=os.read(self.master,65536)
                except OSError:break
                if not chunk:break
                data+=chunk
        return data
    def key(self,s):
        os.write(self.master,s)
        return self.read()
    def test_help_setup_and_persistent_toggle(self):
        self.assertIn(b'Released under the GNU GPLv2+',self.key(b'h'))
        self.key(b' ')
        self.assertIn(b'Categories',self.key(b'S'))
        self.key(b'\x1b')
        self.key(b'H')
        self.key(b'q')
        self.assertEqual(self.process.wait(timeout=3),0)
        self.assertIn('hide_userland_threads=1',self.rc.read_text())
    def test_filter_prompt(self):
        self.assertIn(b'Filter:',self.key(b'\\'))
        self.key(b'this-process-is-not-present')
        self.key(b'\r')
        self.assertIsNone(self.process.poll())
        self.key(b'\\')
        self.key(b'\x1b')
        self.key(b'q')
        self.assertEqual(self.process.wait(timeout=3),0)
    def test_send_signal(self):
        self.assertIn(b'Send signal:',self.key(b'k'))
        self.key(b'\r')
        self.assertEqual(self.child.wait(timeout=3),-15)
        self.key(b'q')
        self.assertEqual(self.process.wait(timeout=3),0)

if __name__=='__main__':unittest.main()
